claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Now I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute towards his upkeep - I help with things like clothes and school expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To better understand your situation:

**Approximately how much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month, and who does Alex currently live with?**

(For reference, Child Benefit rates are currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, which works out to about £110.93 per month)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's needs. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a couple more questions:

**Has Alex's mum claimed Child Benefit for Alex, or are you and she in agreement about who should claim it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his mum hasn't claimed Child Benefit for him. We're fine with me claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances such as being in hospital, in care, or living in residential accommodation for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just living normally with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Age requirement met**: Alex is 8 years old, which is under 16

✓ **Responsibility requirement met**: Although Alex doesn't live with you, you contribute £30 per week towards his upkeep (clothes and school expenses), which is more than the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week. This makes you responsible for him under the Child Benefit rules.

✓ **UK residence**: You live in the UK

✓ **No conflicting claim**: Alex's mum hasn't claimed Child Benefit for him, and you both agree that you should claim it

✓ **No special circumstances**: Alex is not in hospital, care, or residential accommodation

**Next steps**: You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Please note**: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay back some or all of it through your tax return.

Therefore, the claimant meets all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex.
